headline: Avalanche’s MacKinnon, Makar exit game with lower-body injuries
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar both left the Avalanche's latest game with lower-body injuries, and that Colorado, off to an 11-6-2 start, could be without both of its stars for a stretch. The outlet doesn't say how long either might be out.

The Avalanche have earned their record, and our numbers say the team around them is strong. Colorado has generated 55 percent of the expected goals so far this season, a measure of how good the chances were on each side, and it holds at 53 percent at five-on-five. The power play is producing 0.78 expected goals per game, which is where losing MacKinnon and Makar would sting most. The team has also scored 12.7 goals more than its chances would predict, so some of that finishing is likely to cool even with a healthy lineup. The one soft spot is goaltending: Colorado is 5.1 goals saved below expected, so it has been leaning on offense to cover for its goalies. Without two stars driving that offense, the margin gets thinner. We'd watch the power play first.
